title: Team Access Lifecycle sketches and decisions
summary: Low-fi wireframes and interaction decisions for org/team membership lifecycle: invites, role changes, API key creation/rotation, service account provisioning, and audit log timelines. Focused on edge cases, keyboard-first flows, and backlog tickets.
body:
Context:
We need a compact, predictable console flow for team/org access management that scales from small startups to enterprise IT. This doc captures sketches, product decisions, and acceptance criteria for the access lifecycle surface (invite, role change, removal/archival, API key lifecycle, service account creation/rotation, and audit log investigation UI).

High-level goals:
- Make membership state and last action obvious at glance (pending invites, active, suspended, archived).
- Single place to manage credentials (API keys + service accounts) with clear scope + expiry + rotation reminders.
- Audit logs should support pivoting from an actor to their actions and filtering by resource/route/model.
- Role changes must be reversible (soft-change with 24h grace for accidental removals) and support canary role rollouts for large orgs.
- Keyboard-first and screen-reader friendly by default.

Wireframe notes (low-fi):
1) Team roster view (list + compact cards)
   - Left: compact team list (searchable) + filters (role, status, last active).
   - Center: roster table/virtualized list with columns: avatar, name, email, role (drop-down), status badge (active/pending/suspended), last activity, primary credential (API key or service account last used).
   - Right: detail panel that slides out for the selected member showing: membership history timeline (invite, role changes, last login, credential issuance), device list (if available), and quick actions (revoke access, suspend, rotate key).
   - Interaction: changing a role opens a micro-confirm modal that summarizes downstream effects (e.g., loss of certain console routes) and offers a 24h undo.

2) Invite flow (single & bulk)
   - Single invite: inline email input with suggested role dropdown and optional expiry (default 30d for contractors). Show warning if inviting domain outside org.
   - Bulk invite: CSV upload with mapping step. On upload, show validation results (duplicates, invalid emails). Create a transient "pending invites" group tile so admins can bulk re-send or cancel.

3) Role templates and inheritance
   - Allow admins to create reusable role-templates (e.g., "Support Reader", "Model Ops Writer") with fine-grained scope: org-wide, team-limited, or resource-limited (route/model level).
   - In roster view indicate if role is direct or inherited from a template (chip). Editing a template triggers a two-step rollout: preview affected members + staged rollout (canary %).

4) API Keys & Service Accounts page (single credential surface)
   - Top-level list grouped by owner (human vs service-account). Each credential row shows: name, type (API key/service account key), scopes, created, last used, expiry, health (stale/not used in 90d), and a rotate/revoke button.
   - Creation flow: choose owner (person or service account), choose scopes (with suggested presets), set expiry & automatic rotation policy, optional pinned IP/CIDR, and human-readable purpose.
   - Rotation UX: when rotating, create new key and mark old as "scheduled to expire" with a grace period. Provide one-click rollout notes to update SDK snippets with the new key ID.
   - Sticky decision: do not allow raw secret preview more than once on create. Provide a copy-to-clipboard ephemeral modal and require an entropy-confirm check (type credential name).

5) Service account creation flow
   - Two paths: quick-create (recommended) and advanced (for custom roles / external kube/air-gapped).
   - Quick create: name, role-template attach, optional expiry, optional key auto-rotation (enable). The UI generates a key bundle and displays provisioning commands (k8s secret manifest, docker-credential helper).
   - Advanced: grants ability to upload public key for keyless auth, attach external identity providers, and configure HSM-backed key storage (enterprise only).

6) Audit log explorer (investigation-first)
   - Timeline primary UX: top-level time-series histogram of events (by count) with heatmap by action type. Below: event list (actor, action, resource, timestamp, ip, result).
   - Pivoting: click actor to filter to their actions; click resource (e.g., API key-id) to see related events; click a model or route to see recent configuration changes.
   - Quick correlation: show "related events" panel for the selected event (e.g., if a key was rotated, show create/rotate/revoke events near that time).
   - Retention toggles for enterprise: show retention policy and link to request extended retention.

Edge cases and decisions:
- Pending invites with duplicate emails: treat as single invite thread; admin can merge and resend with a note attached.
- Membership suspension vs removal: suspension keeps the member in roster with a suspended badge; removal archives them and moves to "archived members" with retention for 90 days.
- Role rollback: allow undo of last role change within 24h; beyond that require explicit change with reason logged in audit.
- API key preview: only shown once. Never store previewable secret. If rotated, show key ID and last used but not prior secret.
- Service account delegation: allow delegation to teams so a service account can be centrally owned but used by multiple teams. Audit logs must attribute actions to {service-account}@team.

Accessibility + keyboard notes:
- All primary actions reachable via keyboard with consistent focus order. Use skip-to-roster link for screen readers.
- Modal confirmations must trap focus and expose accessible names for screen readers; micro-confirm wording should not rely on color or placement.

Backlog items to create (initial ticket set):
- PLAT-1378: Implement roster virtualized table + slide-out detail panel (acceptance criteria below).
- PLAT-1379: Bulk invite CSV mapping UI + validation engine.
- PLAT-1380: Credential lifecycle service (rotation scheduling, grace windows).
- PLAT-1381: Audit log pivot UI + related-events correlation.
- PLAT-1382: Role-template management + canary rollout engine.

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- Roster view shows status, role, last activity, and primary credential for each member; selecting a member opens detail slide-out with timeline (must match events in audit log for that member).
- Single invite flow validates email, enforces default expiry policy, and creates a pending invite that is visible in the pending invites panel.
- Credential creation flow requires a one-time secret preview and enforces copy/confirm text; rotate flow schedules expiration and keeps old key usable during grace period.
- Audit explorer allows filtering by actor/resource/time-range and supports click-to-pivot behavior.

Privacy/security considerations:
- Do not expose full secrets in logs; store only key IDs and masked references.
- Provide an enterprise-only toggle to require HSM-backed keys for service accounts.
- For SSO-managed orgs, disable password reset and show a clear banner explaining actions delegated to IdP.

Mockups & next steps:
- Convert low-fi sketches to a single Figma file (linked in linked_artifacts). Attach main frames: roster-list, invite flow, credential flow, audit explorer.
- UX: run a quick moderated session with two customers (one early-stage startup, one regulated mid-market) to validate default expiry choices and rotation messaging. Target 2-week turnaround.
- Engineering: spike on the credential lifecycle storage model (rotate in-place vs. shadow key approach).

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
1) Should the default API key expiry be 30d or 90d? 30d is safer but has higher friction for stable infra. Proposal: default 30d for human user keys, 90d for service accounts with rotation recommended.
2) Soft undo window on role changes: 24h seems reasonable but can we make it configurable per-org? Likely enterprise-only toggle.
3) How tightly do we tie role-templates to resource-level scoping? Full resource scoping increases complexity but unlocks fine-grained permissions for bigger customers. Consider MVP with team-level + org-level only, resource scoping in phase 2.

Notes to designers/engineers:
- Keep UI density moderate; teams often have hundreds of members — use virtualization and server-side pagination.
- Instrument telemetry for "role change frequency", "credential rotation rate", and "audit pivot usage". These will feed product decisions.

Done-by suggestions and timelines:
- Wireframes -> hi-fi frames in Figma: 2sprint (design + review).
- Frontend implementation (roster + slide-out): 3 sprints (includes accessibility pass).
- Backend (credential lifecycle + audit pivots): 3-4 sprints depending on integration with existing audit index.

Contact for clarifications: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai) — include product requirements channel #prod-console in Slack when creating tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Roster shows status, role, last activity, primary credential and detail timeline on slide-out
Invite flow validates email and creates visible pending invite
Credential creation enforces one-time secret preview and rotation schedules with grace period
Audit explorer supports filter, pivot, and related-events correlation
